title: Fencing tokens for lease holders
summary: Reject stale lease holders at the resource by checking a monotonically increasing token with each write.
triggers: expired lease holder resumes after another worker takes ownership
resource must reject stale writes from older lease epochs
prompts: A worker pauses and loses its lease. Keep its late write from overwriting a newer worker’s committed result.
Let the current worker write several times during the same lease while rejecting writers from earlier leases.
invariant: The resource compares and updates its highest seen token and value atomically. A rejected write leaves both untouched.
mantra: Fence at the resource, on every write.
pitfalls: The lease service must issue increasing tokens in the resource’s scope; random tokens do not establish order.
The check must be atomic with the write, and the resource must persist the highest token if the guard must survive restarts.
The register cannot infer lease expiry. It rejects an old holder only after seeing a higher token.

anchors.name: Paused lease holder
anchors.trick: A client-side expiry check cannot rule out a pause between that check and the write.

anchors.name: One token per lease
anchors.trick: Equal tokens represent writes in the same lease; strictly smaller tokens are stale.

mutations.explanation: This also rejects writes from the current lease. Equality does not make the token stale.
